items.title: Jay-Z to Perform at Apple Music 2027 Super Bowl Halftime Show
items.summary:
Jay-Z will headline the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show on Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood. The rapper and Roc Nation founder has produced the halftime show for the NFL for several years without taking the stage himself; this time he is the performer.

"From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said in a statement. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true." NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said that when the league first struck its deal with Roc Nation, he made one request: "that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him."

The booking caps a year Jay-Z spent marking three decades in music under the Jay-Z 30 banner. He headlined the Roots Picnic in late May, played three sold-out nights at Yankee Stadium in July tied to the anniversaries of The Blueprint and Reasonable Doubt, performed in Paris and London, and sat with Rick Rubin for the eight-part docuseries Jay-Z in 8. He closed the run last weekend at SoFi Stadium across two nights with guests including Scarface, DJ Khaled, John Legend, Blue Ivy Carter, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short.

Roc Nation will executive produce the halftime show and Hamish Hamilton will direct, Variety reported. The game will air on ESPN, ABC and Disney+, with mobile streaming via NFL+, a Spanish-language ESPN telecast on ESPN Deportes and Disney+, and a separate Spanish-language presentation on Univision.

Apple's vice president of music and international content, Oliver Schusser, pointed to the company's work with Jay-Z on previous halftime bookings, saying, "we are so thrilled that he will be taking that stage himself this year." The most recent show, Bad Bunny's Puerto Rico-themed performance, drew an average of 128.2 million viewers, ahead of the game's 124.9 million but short of the 133.5 million Kendrick Lamar reached in 2025. Bad Bunny's halftime set won seven Emmys last month, including outstanding special (live).

items.title: David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience ‘Stage’ From Brett Morgen to World Premiere at Berlin Film Festival
items.summary:
The David Bowie immersive concert experience Stage will hold its world premiere Feb. 14 at Berlin's Uber Arena, playing as part of the Berlin Film Festival. The production is built around recently discovered and restored footage from Bowie's 1978 Isolar II World Tour, the run that featured material from Heroes.

Documentary filmmaker Brett Morgen found the original camera negatives while making his Grammy-winning Bowie film Moonage Daydream. Stage is a collaboration between Morgen, the David Bowie Estate and Wonderworld, the company founded by former AEG International president Rob Hallett, presented in association with the Berlinale.

Variety reported that the show uses a three-screen setup combining large-scale projections with transparent LED screens, plus a lighting design by Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include the Rolling Stones and Elton John. The audio comes from Academy Award winner Paul Massey, who mixed Bohemian Rhapsody, Michael and Moonage Daydream, working in 7.1 surround and spatial audio to place the audience inside the concert.

Berlinale director Tricia Tuttle called the premiere "like a dream come true: Bowie, Brett Morgen, a world-class sound and light team all coming together in the city's premiere music arena," noting Berlin's long association with Bowie. Hallett said the team is "ensuring this experience is 100% faithful to his legacy while making his genius accessible to global fans and a new generation."

The booking marks an unusual move into alternative programming for the festival, which rarely stages events outside conventional film screenings. Morgen will also appear as a headline speaker in the talks program at the Berlinale's European Film Market, with further details expected in the coming weeks.

items.title: Factory Floor Return With First Album in 10 Years
items.summary:
Factory Floor, the London electronic group that put out its debut on DFA in 2013, has announced One Trip, its first album in a decade. The record arrives Nov. 27 on Erol Alkan's Phantasy Sound, led by the double single "Continuation" / "One Trip."

The band is now a trio of original members Nik Colk Void and Gabe Gurnsey plus new addition Joe Ward. Founding member Dominic Butler left before the group's second album, 25 25, in 2016, after which Void and Gurnsey continued releasing music on labels including Editions Mego and Phantasy Sound, the latter of which has issued a run of recent singles leading into the new record.

Pitchfork reported that Factory Floor resurfaced as a live act in 2024 at Mutek Festival. "We felt an appetite to work in a space where artists could connect emotionally and physically, both in the studio and on a live stage," the group said in a press release after that show. "These environments hold more than sound; they carry a visceral energy that comes from being together. It's something we'd really missed as solo artists, and it made us want to explore that kind of experience again."

One Trip runs 10 tracks: "Continuation," "Big Brain," "DruuuuM," "One Trip," "Buzz Saw," "Between You," "One Two One," "Obsessed," "Souuuu:D" and "Greedy." The group will debut a new live show at London's Barbican on Dec. 5, supporting Squid.
